# Worlds Within

> Worlds Within is one persistent world played through many genres, and the engine that makes it. The repo is LLM-first: content is text, every run is repeatable from a seed, and tools let an agent check its own work. The engine (`engine/`) holds the loop, input, audio, graphics data, the presentation contract and backends; kits (`kits/`) hold one genre's gameplay rules and never draw (they describe each frame and a backend draws it through the game's skin); games (`games/`) hold content and depend on the engine and kits, never the other way round. Start with `CLAUDE.md` at the root, then the page for the module you are changing.

## Project

- [Root agent instructions](CLAUDE.md): rules every change must follow, and the checks to run before pushing
- [Design](docs/DESIGN.md): what the engine and the game are, and the dependency rule
- [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md): the release plan; check it before adding features
- [Stacking-test gap report](docs/reports/stacking-test.md): what Engine 0.7's test game found missing, 37 gaps, each fixed (20 in 0.7, 3 more in 0.10) or moved to a named release, plus the glue review
- [Mini-siege gap report](docs/reports/mini-siege.md): what Engine 0.11's multi-genre sample (an RTS siege with a top-down mission, played or delegated) finds missing, each gap fixed or moved to a named release, plus the glue review; from Engine 0.13 M13 fixed and the dawn follow-up's gaps M29-M36 (fixed, or moved to 0.15); from Engine 0.14 M19 fixed (the round recorder), and the data-only ridge camp's gaps M37 (fixed) and M38 (save codes and new missions, moved to 0.15)
- [Tower-defense lessons report](docs/reports/tower-defense.md): what Engine 0.12's platform test (a new tower-defense mode added with no `engine/sim` change) needs elsewhere, with the empty `engine/sim` diff, 14 lessons for the mission API (ids `D1`-`D14`, each moved to the 0.15 API review or to 1.0) and the glue review; no stacking-test or mini-siege gap is assigned to 0.12

## Modules

- [engine/core](docs/modules/engine-core.md): loop, scenes, input (keyboard, gamepad, touch pad, and from Engine 0.9 pointer gestures for mouse and touch: tap, box, pan, zoom), audio and MML, save, seeded RNG, maths, the renderer contract, the kit hook (`KitDef`), the mini game hook (`MiniGameDef` with an optional `paramsSchema` and `report()`, `miniGameScene`), the headless game contract (with optional recorded `order`s and, from Engine 0.10, the game's `miniGames` for `validate`), the RTS order and unit-type data shared by the sim and kits (`orders.ts`, `rts-types.ts`), `minigame-params.ts` (Engine 0.10: level trigger and mission params checked against the mini game's schema), and from Engine 0.10 the mission contract (`missions.ts`: mission definitions and the `mission` content kind with a fixed world-time cost, declared outcomes with delegation weights and data-only effects, structured results and reports, opportunity windows, committed records, `MissionAdapter`, and `mission-adapter.ts`: `playMissionRound` plays a mission through a kit's mini game and maps its report to a declared outcome), and `campaign.ts` (the `campaign` content kind: the order a game plays its levels or missions in, as data); from Engine 0.11 a round's own input map and host HUD keys (`MiniGameDef.inputMap`, `hostStatus`, `RoundInput`: a button held into a round is ignored until released), `checkUse` for params checks that need the content, and `MissionHost` (`mission-host.ts`): live hosting of a game's missions over a `MissionWorldPort`, the round stepped while the world waits, then the world stepped on so the result commits at its fixed tick; the headless contract's optional `mission(step)` and `missionExperience()`; from Engine 0.13 the `fate` effect and choice missions without `play`, `fateState` / `isLost` for kits reading a snapshot, campaigns played in order with `{ scenario, ticks }` entries (`campaignRun`, `advanceCampaign`), campaign saves (`campaignSaveSchema`, `save/campaign-store.ts`), the carried record's schemas (`carried.ts`), save codes (`campaign-code.ts`: versioned, CRC-16 checked Crockford Base32) and the headless contract's optional `campaignSave()`; from Engine 0.14 a run file's `start` (`HeadlessOptions.start`, `starts(content)`, `campaignSaveAt`), per-kit rule ids (`disabledRulesByKit`, `rulesOffFor`), the read-only world hooks `worldEvents(sinceTick)` and `timeline()`, the round recorder (`InputRecorder`, `recordRounds`/`roundRecordings`, kits' `roundBots`) and the shared state hash (`state-hash.ts`)
- [engine/core/content](docs/modules/engine-core-content.md): content files read and checked with Zod schemas: text grids, song, sfx, sprite and palette schemas, game manifests (with the picture size, `screen`) and the content loader, errors naming the file and field
- [engine/core/present](docs/modules/engine-core-present.md): the presentation contract: the read-only per-frame snapshot (`PresentFrame`: entities, map, events, HUD status, camera and other extension points) a kit hands a backend, the `Presenter` interface, `freezeFrame`, `MapTracker`, the `presentFrameSchema` Zod schema, skin files (the `skin` content kind and `resolveSkinFrame`; `three` skins with text-defined low-poly meshes and `camera3d`), eight-way `Facing` (Engine 0.9), `CameraFollower`, the camera framing maths both backends share, `RtsCamera` (Engine 0.9: a scrolling, zooming camera over a map larger than the screen, with screen-to-world maths for pointer input), and `FrameStream` / `PendingEvents` / `FramePicture`, the per-frame stream from a world and its events to frozen frames; from Engine 0.11 a skin kind's `byTag` looks (`resolveSkinKind`) and event sounds keyed by result or field (`mini-game-end:pass`, `mission-commit:outcome=...`, `resolveSkinEvent`)
- [engine/core/shell](docs/modules/engine-core-shell.md): the browser shell games share: `?backend=` choice and the 2D/3D toggle, `HostScene` (plays a headless game and pushes its mini games), `bootBrowserGame` (keyboard, gamepad, touch pad, optional pointer gestures, scene stack, fixed loop, and from Engine 0.11 an `audio` option: sfx and songs unlocked on the first key, tap or click, music, each display's `onSound`) over a display a backend builds; `HostScene` also hosts a game's mission rounds (Engine 0.11); `CampaignSession` (Engine 0.13: an entry's end stored and packed into a save code, a typed code resumed); from Engine 0.14 a manual-loop mode with the `window.__ww` step hook (`step(n)`, `tick`, `snapshot()`, `hash()`, `replay(runFile)`, `?debug=step`) and `?record` to record a hosted round's input
- [engine/backends/canvas2d](docs/modules/engine-backends-canvas2d.md): the browser 2D backend, viewport, `SkinnedCanvasPresenter` (draws presentation frames through a skin, honouring the camera's zoom from Engine 0.9) and `canvasDisplay`, the page's 2D display
- [engine/backends/three](docs/modules/engine-backends-three.md): the 3D backend: `ThreeScene` builds a side-on 2.5D Three.js scene (instanced tile blocks, entity meshes by id, a perspective camera framed like the 2D one) from presentation frames and a `three` skin, testable in Node; `threeDisplay` (the page's 3D display, or why WebGL 2 is missing) and `threeScenePresenter` (a Node-side `Presenter`)
- [engine/backends/null](docs/modules/engine-backends-null.md): the headless backend that draws nothing (`NullRenderer`, `NullPresenter`)
- [engine/sim](docs/modules/engine-sim.md): the headless, deterministic world simulation (Engine 0.8): entities, components, fixed-order systems, a seeded RNG and an integer tick (one world minute); standard components, terrain with height and squads with named members; an event log of every committed change with its cause; save and load of the whole world as JSON; world scenarios as data and the sample village world; from Engine 0.9, in-house 8-way A\* and flow fields, RTS orders applied between ticks (`applyOrder`) and the RTS systems (movement, combat, construction, training, one gatherable resource) in a named system set (`"systems": "rts"`), with a recorded battle fixture; from Engine 0.10, time (`time.ts`: world, experience and commitment time, frozen events that hold a battle still while construction goes on), missions (`mission.ts`: open, delegate by a weighted draw or play, commit at a fixed world-time cost with data-only effects and append-only records, no retries) and opportunities (`opportunity.ts`: windows that open and close in world time, taking one can close another), with the siege fixture and its mission run files; from Engine 0.11 `missionPort(world, { refs })`, the port an engine `MissionHost` hosts a world's missions through; and deterministic integer and fixed-point maths (`math.ts`) in place of machine-dependent float maths; from Engine 0.13 fates of named people (`fate.ts`: injured, captured, freed, dead, forward only; the dead and captured kept as records off the map) and carry-over (`carry.ts`: a scenario's `from`, `carriedRecord`, `worldFromScenario(json, { carried })`), with the captive fixtures and their run files; from Engine 0.14 the timeline record (`timeline.ts`: `timelineOf` over a world's snapshot and event log: world clock, frozen spans, experience, opportunity windows with their history, committed missions) and `missionPort`'s `events` and `timeline`
- [engine/tools](docs/modules/engine-tools.md): the CLI for agents and people (`pnpm cli help`): validate content (from Engine 0.10 also each level trigger's and mission's mini game params, and each `campaign` file's level and mission ids), play run files headless with tick assertions, invariants and state hashes (and, from Engine 0.9, recorded orders with sync hashes, so a battle replays to the same hashes; from Engine 0.10, world runs open, delegate, play or quit missions from data, report refused steps and experience ticks, and commit each at its fixed world tick), write replay files for failing runs (with hash-mismatch checks), dump the state at a tick (of a game, or of a sim world from a `world` run file), edit content with get/set/add/remove (every write schema-checked and verified), mutant checks that switch kit rules off to find weak run files, from Engine 0.11 game runs open, delegate, play (with the round's recorded input) or quit missions through the game's `mission` step; deterministic PNG screenshots of a run at a tick (with the run's mission steps) (headless Chromium; `--backend three` for 3D, refusing software WebGL unless `--allow-software-gl`), with one JSON result per command and grouped exit codes; from Engine 0.13 game run files that start `from` another run or a save code and pin `codes`, and the `code` command (a run's save code); from Engine 0.14 `trace` (a few paths over a range of ticks), a run file's `start` (a level or campaign entry), `kit:id` rule ids and per-kit mutants, `get --ruler` and `paste` region edits for text maps, `events`, `timeline` and `dump --out` (the world's event log and timeline as data), `record` (a hosted round's input into a `play` step, from the page or the kit's bot) and `debug` (the in-browser debugger; a failing run prints the line that opens its replay at the failing tick)
- [engine/tools/debugger](docs/modules/engine-tools-debugger.md): the in-browser simulation debugger (Engine 0.14): `pnpm cli debug <run, replay or dump file>` serves a tools-only page (never in the Pages build) showing the world state (tree, search, diff from the previous tick), the event log with filters, the run's checks and hashes against the golden file and the game's picture, stepping forward and rewinding by re-simulating from tick 0; `--check` opens it in headless Chromium and compares the page's hash with the headless run's; `window.__wwDebugger` for tests; a timeline viewer (world clock, frozen spans, opportunity windows, mission opens and commits, clickable) and replays opened at their failing tick with the failed check and the tick before (Engine 0.14 T11)
- [kits/topdown](docs/modules/kits-topdown.md): gameplay rules for a room-based top-down action game, with named rules a run can switch off; `presentWorld` describes each frame (map, entities, HUD status, events, camera hint); `roomChallenge` hosts one room as a mini game whose `report()` (Engine 0.10) says what was beaten and who was hurt; from Engine 0.11 `missionRoom` and `topdownMissionAdapter` (`mission-room`) play a mission over a world as one room, all from the mission's params (world entities by selector into foe slots, ordered rules from the report to an outcome), tagging each foe with its world name; from Engine 0.13 a round's hero taken from a world unit (`hero: { select, hpPer }`, `heroHpLost`) and selectors that skip the captured and the dead; the kit never draws
- [kits/platformer](docs/modules/kits-platformer.md): gameplay rules for a side-scrolling platformer: `level` files (a JSON header plus a `.map.txt` text grid) and physics `profile` files in whole sub-pixel units with data-set actor types; integer physics and level objects as named rules (strict mutant checks), golden traces against SMBC, mini-game triggers, level sequences in id order or a `campaign` file's order; presentation frames (`presentWorld`); the kit never draws
- [kits/rts](docs/modules/kits-rts.md): the real-time strategy kit (Engine 0.9): reads a plain `engine/sim` world snapshot, turns click and box selection and commands into orders, runs a scripted enemy written as data, and describes each frame (map, units with eight-way facing, buildings and construction, selection, HUD, camera); from Engine 0.11 mission offers and open missions read from the snapshot, the launch command (`missionButtons`, `launchMission`, carried out by a `MissionHost`), `frozen` and `damaged` tags, the offer marker and mission HUD, `sidesOf`, and `rts-map` opportunities; from Engine 0.13 named people with their fate and the `captive` status, the captured and the dead gone from the view; no world rules, no drawing, no sim import
- [kits/towerdefense](docs/modules/kits-towerdefense.md): the tower-defense kit (Engine 0.12, the platform test): `td-map` files (a JSON header plus a `.map.txt` grid: one path from entry to exit, build cells, blocked ground; starting gold and lives), `td-towers` tables and `td-waves` lists; a headless, deterministic round (`TdWorld`: place and sell towers for gold, waves by button or timer, enemies walking the path in whole sub-cell units, towers targeting the enemy furthest along with cooldowns, bounties, leaks costing lives, won or lost) with every rule named for mutant checks (strict); `TdControls` (a cursor on the shared actions, pointer taps to cells), presentation frames (`tdFrames`, `td-*` events for sounds), the headless `tdGame` and a small `TdBot`; the `td-defence` mini game and `towerdefenseMissionAdapter`, a data-driven mission over a world played as one round (world walls on the build cells, the gold from a stockpile, the wave from world units, ordered rules from the report to a declared outcome; from Engine 0.13 the selectors skip the captured and the dead); no world rules, no drawing, no sim import
- [games/samples/dungeon](docs/modules/games-samples-dungeon.md): the top-down dungeon sample (the old demo, moved here in Engine 0.15): three rooms on the top-down kit, drawn by the Canvas2D backend through its skin (`content/skins/canvas2d.json`)
- [games/platformer-lab](docs/modules/games-platformer-lab.md): the platformer kit's test lab: the kit's fixture level and five rule levels played in turn, run files that guard every kit rule, a placeholder Canvas2D skin and a low-poly 3D skin (`?backend=three` plays it through the Three.js backend), and a tiny test mini game
- [games/samples/rts-skirmish](docs/modules/games-samples-rts-skirmish.md): the first RTS sample (Engine 0.9): one map as a world scenario, unit and building types, a scripted raiding party as data, text pixel art and a Canvas2D skin, on `kits/rts` over `engine/sim`; run files build a barracks, train soldiers and beat the raid from recorded orders (and through interface actions) with sync hashes
- [games/samples/mini-siege](docs/modules/games-samples-mini-siege.md): the multi-genre sample (Engine 0.11): a village under attack on `kits/rts` over `engine/sim` and one top-down mission (`kits/topdown`'s data-driven `mission-room`, hosted by `engine/core`'s `MissionHost`) to burn the siege engines, played or delegated; run files for both paths (played, delegated, quit) show the frozen battle, the watchtower finishing during it, the commit at the fixed tick and the outcome's effects; original NES-style text art, two Canvas2D skins, sfx and one MML song, and a page (`games/samples/mini-siege/`) where the mission is launched, then played or delegated; from Engine 0.12 a tower-defense preparation phase (`fortify`, the towerdefense kit's `td-defence` on the real walls with the village's gold against the real raiders, played or delegated, its losses written back to the world) with its own run files, art and skin; from Engine 0.13 a campaign of two scenarios: the captain as the sabotage's hero, captured when it is driven off, then "The dawn assault", which starts from the siege's results (his fate and hp, the gold) and plays differently when he was taken (rescue, exchange or leave him), with save codes on the page and in run files (`dawn-*`); from Engine 0.14 a third scenario added with data files only, "The ridge camp" (`ridge-raid`, started with `start: { entry: "ridge" }`), the Done when's proof in the debugger, and the played rounds recorded with `pnpm cli record`
- [games/samples/tower-defense](docs/modules/games-samples-tower-defense.md): the standalone tower-defense sample (Engine 0.12, the platform test): one winding road, arrow and cannon towers and three waves as data on `kits/towerdefense`, with no `engine/sim`; run files place towers with the cursor, hold every wave or lose to a thin defence, and guard every kit rule (the kit is strict); original NES-style text art, a Canvas2D skin, sfx and one MML song, and a page (`games/samples/tower-defense/`) played with keys, the touch pad or taps
- [games/samples/platformer](docs/modules/games-samples-platformer.md): the platformer sample (the Engine 0.7 stacking test, moved here in Engine 0.15): a small original platformer on the platformer kit that finds what the engine is missing: four short levels and a door that pushes a top-down room challenge over the level, playable in 2D and 3D; a worked example of a game on two kits

## Reference

- [API cheat sheet](docs/CHEATSHEET.md): one page of the public API: a game's folder, booting a game, content kinds, the headless contract, run files and the CLI loop (its tables are generated)
- [CLI reference](docs/reference/cli.md): every command's help, exactly as `pnpm cli help` prints it (generated)
- [Schema reference](docs/reference/schemas.md): every file format (game manifest, run files, each content kind) with fields, types, defaults, limits and an example (generated)
- [Skills](docs/modules/skills.md): agent skills for common jobs, and how to add one

## Skills

- [Scaffold a game](.claude/skills/scaffold-game/SKILL.md): make a new one-room game in `games/<name>/` that passes `validate`, `run` and the four checks
- [Debug a failing run](.claude/skills/debug-failing-run/SKILL.md): from a failing `run` to its first failing tick, the replay in the debugger at that tick, dumps, screenshot, replay and mutant checks, then fix and rerun
